messages:
Alex (customer): Hi team — intermittently seeing embeddings come back with the wrong dimensionality. Our ingest fails because our table expects 1024 floats but occasionally receives 1536. Happened across multiple requests. Example response payload: 
{
  "error": "dimension_mismatch",
  "expected": 1024,
  "received": 1536
}
Any idea what could cause mixed dims from the embeddings endpoint? We're calling /v1/embeddings without specifying model param.

Eva (support): Thanks @Alex, escalating. Customer account acct_0x9c. Sample request ids: r_1971004323, r_1971004350, r_1971004389. Noted they switched SDKs and removed explicit model name. Posting the curl example they used: 

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input": ["a", "b"] }'
```

Eva (support): They also pasted the client error from their DB layer: 
"insert failed: vector length 1536 != expected 1024"

Jay (support-lead): Looping in runtime and ML infra: @Li @Ravi — could this be routing selecting different model variants and batcher mixing them? If batcher merges requests for different embed variants, that could explain sporadic wrong dims and tail latency when batches wait for slower variants. Can you fetch the batcher logs for those request IDs?

Li (eng-runtime): Pulling logs now. Quick context: we have two embedding models active: redwood-embed-1024 (stable) and redwood-embed-v2 (1536). For requests without model_hint, router can pick either based on load/region. Found relevant snippets: 

```
[1971004323] queue.push: tenant=acct_0x9c, model_hint=none, route=preferred:embed-1024
[1971004323] batcher.coalesce -> batch_id=embed-cohort-27, variants_seen={embed-1024}
[1971004350] queue.push: tenant=acct_0x9c, model_hint=none, route=selected:embed-v2
[1971004350] batcher.coalesce -> batch_id=embed-cohort-27, variants_seen={embed-1024, embed-v2}
[1971004350] batcher.flush batch_id=embed-cohort-27 size=12 latency=310ms
[1971004350] infer executed model=embed-v2 output_dim=1536
[1971004350] response sent dim=1536
[1971004389] ingest failed dimension_mismatch expected=1024 received=1536
```

Li (eng-runtime): TL;DR: the cohort key currently groups by tenant+family but not by output_dim, so the batcher happily coalesces requests destined for different variants. When the batch flush uses embed-v2, everyone in the batch got 1536-dim vectors. Also the flush latency shows ~310ms — that aligns with customer's tail latency reports during mixed traffic.

Ravi (ml-eng): Confirmed. We recently adjusted routing probabilities to favor v2 under heavier loads; without explicit model in the request, some percent of requests hit v2. I reproduced locally with a traffic mix test (90% -> embed-1024, 10% -> embed-v2) and batch_timeout 200ms. Outcome: ~1% of requests returned 1536 dims, and tail latency spiked whenever batches waited for the v2 selection to arrive. Repro script I used: 

```
for i in $(seq 1 2000); do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"input": "sample '"$i"'" }' &
  sleep 0.005
done
wait
```

Ravi (ml-eng): Root cause: cohort key missing output_dim; router occasionally selects a different-dim variant; batcher coalesces across variants and then one model executes, causing dimension mismatch and tail latency.

Jay (support-lead): Need immediate mitigation for the customer and a longer-term fix. Short-term: advise customer to set model="redwood-embed-1024" in their requests to pin the dimension, or modify their DB to accept 1536. Anything we can toggle server-side quickly?

Li (eng-runtime): We can enable a tenant-scoped config strict_dim_check that prevents coalescing across differing output dimensions (it will flush batches separately if a new-dim request arrives). It's a config flip and safe to canary. Downsides: slightly higher CPU/throughput cost due to smaller batches. I can flip it for acct_0x9c immediately as a canary.

deploy-bot: rollout started: config/embeddings/batcher/strict_dim_check=true for tenant acct_0x9c (canary) 1:45 UTC  deploy_id=dpl_1971004450

ingest-bot: correlated trace created tr_0xdef456 for r_1971004350 batch_id=embed-cohort-27 region=us-east-1

Eva (support): Messaging to customer: 
- Short-term options: set model parameter to "redwood-embed-1024" or permit 1536 vectors in your DB.
- We've applied a tenant canary (strict_dim_check=true) to avoid cross-dim coalescing for your account; monitoring now.
- ETA: if canary looks good over 30 minutes we'll promote wider.

Alex (customer): Thanks. We'll pin model and coordinate with DB team. Please notify when global fix is rolled.

Ravi (ml-eng): Proposed long-term fixes (ticket INF-4580): 
1) Add output_dim to batcher cohort key so variants with different output sizes never coalesce.
2) Make router prefer explicit model_hint strongly (if client provided model param, don't override).
3) Emit per-tenant embedding_dim metrics and alert on mixed-dim batches.
4) Add regression test in CI that simulates mixed-variant routing and fails if cross-dim coalescing occurs.

Jay (support-lead): Action items: 
- Li: monitor canary and promote to global default if stable (ETA 3h).
- Ravi: implement cohort key change + tests (INF-4580, ETA 2w).
- Eva: keep customer updated and close support thread when customer confirms pinning.

Li (eng-runtime): Acknowledged. I'll prepare a short postmortem and follow-up once INF-4580 starts.

Eva (support): Marking support side resolved pending customer confirmation. Will re-open if customer sees further issues. :thumbsup:
